configuration.rebuild_requirement: On this topic the loss is downstream of retrieval, not in it: of the 33 Goodman rows we did not pool, 28 were retrieved by our own hand-written queries and then lost -- 13 at screening (X2 x10, X1 x2, X3 x1) and 15 at extraction (SOURCE_NOT_RETRIEVED x10, EXTRACTION_NOT_PERFORMED x3, REFUSED_ON_EVIDENCE x2); 0 were reachable only beyond the rank-650 cap; 0 were missed by all three hand-written queries but returned by the concept query; 0 resolved PubMed rows were in none of the measured sources; 5 citations could not be resolved to a PMID by title esearch (indexing NOT observed -- not 'not indexed'). Corpus-v1 must fix, in this order: (1) screening -- the X2 population rule reads only title/conditions and rejects AAD trials whose titles do not name AAD, and X1 reads registry pubtype as the RCT test; (2) extraction -- an included trial whose abstract lacks arm counts is left unpooled because full text is not fetched; (3) search -- a registered, fully paginated concept+registry search replaces the three hand-written strings, which on this topic was not the binding loss.

Each is rewritten to the property it protected. A test that asserts a finding will defend that finding against the evidence. INCIDENT on the countersignature file (2026-09-21 ~10:35Z, before signing): a shell heredoc collapsed the backslashes in a patch script, the patch failed, and a ';'-chained probe on the same command line ran the PRE-patch countersign script on esketamine with '--by X' and no basis, writing a signature that named no basis into docs/result_changes.json. Caught at once (the probe's own output named the signer), restored from the byte-identical mirror tree, verified 13 OPEN and 0 rendered hashes moved, and only then signed through the patched script with --basis required. Nothing was regenerated or published in between. Recorded because a near-miss on the one file built to be tamper-evident belongs in the ledger; rule adopted: a state-changing command is never chained after a patch with ';'.

executable_evidence.topic_list: Demonstrated on the named topic colchicine-recurrent-pericarditis (lane E2b's end-to-end construction: real offline families writer -> empty certified map -> fresh build -> full gate PASS before the fix; non-empty-but-incomplete control -> GATE REFUSE) and on the synthetic fixture topic in tests/test_admission_enforced.py. The check itself is corpus-wide: it runs on 32 of 32 served pages, every page whose certified cache/<slug>/families.json is read.

fixes.class: The signing surface for the 41 OPEN result-change notices: a presenter that never signs, a digest the reviewer's signature is bound to, an unambiguous notice selector, and a ledger chain check

executable_evidence.scope_basis: Named behaviours, not corpus numbers: sign --expect-digest REFUSES and writes nothing when the rendered block changed between reading and signing (tested by mutating the notice between the two commands); the legacy substring selector still refuses an ambiguous match while the new exact selector reaches the intended notice, tested on all six real duplicate (slug, outcome) pairs; chain_integrity holds for all 48 outcome groups on 32 of 32 served pages and a planted break refuses; the walker presents ONE notice per invocation, keeps no cursor, emits no signing command for an already-signed notice, and shows D01 as NOT SIGNABLE with no empty slot. Demonstrated across the named topic set of all 32 served pages.
executable_evidence.topic_list: All 32 served pages carry the ledger the walker reads; the six duplicate-pair topics (esketamine-trd-madrs, omega3-cardiovascular-events, pcsk9-mace, probiotics-aad-prevention x3) are the named selector cases.
